# Results — Study 697 (Wolfe Waves)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Bill Wolfe's
five-point converging wedge, whose point-5 "throw-over" past the 1-3 trendline projects a
price-and-time **EPA target** via the 1-4 trendline extended forward. A percentage **ZigZag**
(4% headline) marks the pivots; the falsifiable question is whether the EPA target gets hit
**more often than a same-distance random target** on the same tape. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**
(the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC, auto-adjusted (total-return), public, no key |
| Basket | SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM, ^GSPC, ^IXIC, ^DJI, GLD — broad indices/ETFs, deep daily history |
| As-of | **2026-06-30** |
| Fingerprints | SPY `16694cd9912d` · QQQ `d935154d0960` · DIA `33e3d47bdd3a` · IWM `1f2218a6b7f2` · ^GSPC `cec06bce14e7` · ^IXIC `54d65c6aa4cb` · ^DJI `803513feb661` · GLD `44f6ff1685e4` |
| Detector | 4% percentage **ZigZag** pivots; a Wolfe candidate requires point 5 to pierce the 1-3 trendline (the one universally-cited rule), point 3 to extend the wedge past point 1, and point 4 to sit inside the channel with a lower high / higher low than point 2 |
| Entry / execution | enter the close **one bar after** point 5's ZigZag confirmation (no look-ahead); walk forward on intraday High/Low up to 90 bars for the target-hit test |
| No survivorship | these are broad-index/ETF *price* tapes, not a cross-sectional single-name panel — no surviving-names selection on the Signal axis |

## The headline — does the EPA price target get hit more than a random target?

Pooled across the basket: **3,543** ZigZag pivots → **370** candidate Wolfe waves that pass the
geometry rules.

| ticker | pivots | candidates |
|---|--:|--:|
| SPY | 337 | 44 |
| QQQ | 431 | 56 |
| DIA | 275 | 28 |
| IWM | 381 | 31 |
| ^GSPC | 975 | 114 |
| ^IXIC | 612 | 73 |
| ^DJI | 315 | 33 |
| GLD | 217 | 18 |
| **pooled** | **3,543** | **370** |

Of those 370, **345** are *decided* within 90 bars (target or stop touched first) and **25** time
out (neither touched — excluded from the hit-rate, reported here for completeness).

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| hit rate (target before stop) | **120/345 = 34.8%** (Wilson 95% [29.9%, 40.0%]) |
| **same-distance random-day placebo** — 1,000 draws/ticker | observed **34.8%** vs placebo mean **34.6%** (sd 2.5pp) |
| placebo *z* / *p* | **z = +0.05**, **p = 0.471** |

**The target gets hit almost exactly as often as a random target the same distance away, on a
random day, would.** The pattern's headline claim — that its geometry marks a real reversal
point — does not clear the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar; it does not even separate from the null's *mean*.

## The EPA time target — "no reliable timer"

For the **120 winning trades**, we compare the actual bars-to-hit against the pattern's own
projected time target (point 5's bar + the point-1-to-point-4 bar span — one fixed, ex-ante
convention; Wolfe's "time axis" is described inconsistently across sources, so we test the one
we can state precisely):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean actual bars-to-hit | **21.7** |
| mean projected time-target offset | **52.2** |
| correlation (actual vs projected) | **+0.041** |
| mean absolute error | **40.8 bars** |

A correlation of **0.04** is indistinguishable from zero, and the projection overshoots the
actual resolution time by roughly 2.4× on average. Even on the rare trades that *do* reach the
target, the pattern's own clock is not predicting when.

## Secondary — fixed-horizon directional return (geometry-free)

A simpler cut that doesn't depend on the target/stop levels at all: hold the predicted direction
for a fixed horizon, pooled across the basket (397 candidates with data through the horizon).

| horizon | n | gross (bps) | net (bps) | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | coin placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 397 | −40 | −42 | 47% | −1.74 | **−2.00** | 0.960 |
| 10-day | 397 | −14 | −16 | 50% | −0.46 | −0.48 | 0.673 |
| 20-day | 397 |  −1 |  −3 | 47% | −0.01 | −0.01 | 0.501 |
| 40-day | 397 | +20 | +18 | 47% | +0.35 | +0.37 | 0.359 |

Nothing clears **+t = 2**. If anything, the only borderline number sits at the *wrong* sign
(5-day HAC *t* = −2.00, coin-placebo *p* = 0.96 — a random direction at the same swing points
beats the Wolfe direction 96% of the time at that horizon) — a weak *negative* tilt at the
shortest horizon, not a positive edge. By 40 days it's flat. **No horizon supports the claim.**

## Robustness — the ZigZag threshold sweep

| threshold | candidates | decided | hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 3% | 527 | 500 | 36.0% |
| 4% (headline) | 370 | 345 | 34.8% |
| 5% | 277 | 247 | 36.4% |
| 8% | 118 | 90 | 37.8% |

Flat across every sensible setting — all four cluster within ~3 points of the placebo's ~35%
baseline, with no monotonic trend. This is not a knob that happens to have missed the edge; there
is no edge to find at any reasonable ZigZag threshold.

## SPY-only — the named single tape (lower power, same answer)

| ticker | candidates | decided | hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 44 | 40 | **32.5%** (Wilson [20.1%, 48.0%]) |

Consistent with the pooled result — and the wide interval (44 candidates over 33 years) is itself
the honest reason we pool: a single index can't generate enough Wolfe waves to say much on its
own.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

A deterministic panel builds the wedge from **exact anchor points** (not accumulated per-bar
noise, which would fragment a leg into spurious extra ZigZag pivots) with a tunable planted
reversal after point 5, walked forward with the geometry-free fixed-horizon test (H = 20):

| world | *n* | mean (bps) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | ~30–58/seed | — | mean **−0.76** (sd 1.25) | \|t\| ≥ 2 in **4/20 seeds** |
| planted edge = +0.30 | 43 | **+668** | **+3.95** | **+5.32** |

The null centers modestly below zero (a mild, disclosed selection effect — every entry follows a
required ≥4% favorable move to *confirm* point 5, and small-sample seeds swing around that): mean
*t* stays well under the ±2 bar in aggregate, though 4 of 20 individual seeds cross it in either
direction — reported here in full rather than hidden. A real planted reversal, in contrast, is
unmistakable — **t up to 5.6** across every horizon:

| horizon | *n* | mean (bps) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 43 | +317 | +4.63 | +5.62 |
| 10-day | 43 | +561 | +4.11 | +5.51 |
| 20-day | 43 | +668 | +3.95 | +5.32 |
| 40-day | 43 | +618 | +3.17 | +4.59 |

The detector can clearly find a reversal **when one is actually there** — so the flat real-tape
result is a true negative, not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The EPA target is hit **34.8%** of the time vs a same-distance random-day
  placebo mean of **34.6%** (*z* = +0.05, *p* = 0.471) — the pattern's headline claim does not
  separate from chance. Robust across the ZigZag threshold (36.0%–37.8%, no trend) and confirmed
  by the geometry-free fixed-horizon cut (|*t*| < 2 at every horizon, one borderline **negative**
  tilt at 5 days). A synthetic control proves the harness *would* detect a real planted reversal
  (*t* up to 5.6), so this is a genuine null, not a broken test.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no edge to charge costs against; the target-hit rate matches
  a random target and the directional returns are flat-to-negative. Nothing to deploy.
- **"No reliable timer"? — CONFIRMED.** The pattern's own projected time target correlates
  **+0.04** with when a winning trade actually resolves (MAE 40.8 bars, on trades that average
  21.7 bars to resolution) — a coin flip with extra steps. Even on the minority of trades that
  *do* reach the target, the pattern cannot tell you when.
